entries.title: Testing a More Thoughtful AI Model
entries.description: We are quietly testing Claude Fable, a newer AI model, for a portion of conversations. When selected, it aims to produce more thoughtful, higher-quality answers. You do not need to change any settings. Most conversations continue as usual, and we will use your thumbs up and thumbs down feedback to compare quality. If something feels off, please vote and tell us why.

entries.title: Ask About Any Teacher by Name
entries.description: Luca now recognizes named teachers across the full library (100+ authors), not only a short hand-maintained list. In Auto mode, ask "What did Nayaswami Gyandev say about mantras?" and Luca focuses retrieval on that teacher on the first turn. Ambiguous names (for example a shared surname) fall back to the usual Auto blend rather than guessing. The author list refreshes weekly as the library grows.

entries.title: More Kriya Talks in the Library
entries.description: We added substantial new Kriya audio to Luca: 147 Kriya talks from the Bhaktan files, plus 63 Treasures Talks on Kriya. Ask about Kriya practice, history, or related teachings, and Luca can draw on this expanded material along with the rest of the library.

entries.title: More Relevant Sources, Clearer Limits
entries.description: Luca now sets aside weakly-matched sources so answers lean on genuinely relevant material instead of loosely-related filler. When your filters (libraries, media types, or a focused source or author) leave nothing to match, Luca tells you which filter is limiting the results and suggests broadening it, rather than guessing or inventing quotes.

entries.title: Auto (recommended) Author Selection
entries.description: The Authors filter now defaults to Auto (recommended). For general spiritual questions, Luca still favors Paramhansa Yogananda and Swami Kriyananda, but can also pull from the wider library when helpful. Questions about a specific teacher (for example Asha) automatically focus on that author, and follow-ups can broaden when the conversation makes that appropriate. You can still choose Master and Swami or All authors for a fixed scope. Homepage suggested queries also work correctly with Auto selected.

entries.title: Source Focus
entries.description: You can now focus Luca on a single source, such as a book, chapter, or source family. Choose a source before asking, or click "Focus on this source" after an answer, and Luca will stay focused there until you clear it.

entries.title: More Task Wizards and Streamlined Tools
entries.description: We now have seven task wizards to help you create comprehensive queries. The wizards will help you get started and suggest follow-up tasks to go even further. Click the magic wand in the question input box to get started.

entries.title: Beginner Zoom Session Recordings
entries.description: Recordings of the beginner Zoom sessions are now available. These recordings provide valuable guidance for those new to Luca.

entries.title: Task Wizard
entries.description: New structured task wizards help you create comprehensive research queries and class plans. Click the task buttons above the chat input to get started. The wizards will help you get started and suggest follow-up tasks to go even further.

entries.title: What's New Feature
entries.description: Stay updated with the latest features and improvements. Click the bell icon in the top right button bar to see recent updates.

entries.title: AI Model Selection
entries.description: You can now choose the underlying AI model that generates the answers. Different AI models have different strengths - some are faster, others are more thorough. Different models may interpret questions differently. Some models excel at creative responses, others at factual accuracy. You can experiment to find which model works best for your needs.
